*South Key is conducting a confidential search for a Head of Operations for one of its clients.*

**Head of Operations, Wealth Management Service Delivery** 
Remote (U.S.; Eastern or Central time zone preferred) · Full-time · Reports to the COO 
Starting base salary $150,000 plus bonus

**About the company**

We are a growing operations partner to registered investment advisors. Our team works as an extension of our clients' staff, handling financial planning support, investment operations, new business processing and client service so advisors can focus on their clients and their growth.

**The role**

The Head of Operations is a leadership role, accountable for service delivery, quality, capacity and team performance across all of our client firms. You will lead a remote team of 20+ across client service, investment operations and financial planning, and build the team-lead layer beneath you.

You will stay close to daily operations, but you will lead through your team leads and managers rather than doing the work yourself. This is not a working-supervisor role. Over the next year, you will build an operation that can support significant client growth.

**What you'll do**

Service delivery and quality 
- Own timely, accurate delivery across all operations service lines. 
- Set service standards, quality controls and escalation procedures. 
- Track turnaround times, SLA commitments, errors, NIGOs, rework and client feedback, and fix the root causes of recurring problems. 
- Serve as the senior escalation point for significant delivery issues.

Team leadership 
- Lead, coach and develop team leads and staff with clear responsibilities and performance expectations. 
- Run consistent training, performance reviews and accountability. 
- Partner with recruiting to define staffing needs, interview candidates and onboard new hires. 
- Build career paths, cross-training and backup coverage that support retention.

Capacity and delivery economics 
- Keep a forward-looking 60–90 day view of workload, staffing, skills and available capacity. 
- Measure capacity and put the right staffing structure in place, including team-lead and manager roles, as the business grows. 
- Recommend hiring and resource allocation based on demand, service requirements and financial impact. 
- Balance productivity with quality and sustainable workloads. 
- Make sure new client start dates line up with operational readiness.

Process improvement and onboarding 
- Build, standardize and document core workflows while allowing for differences between client firms. 
- Improve workflows to reduce manual work, errors and unnecessary handoffs, partnering with the technology team on automation and system changes. 
- Own operational readiness for new client engagements: staffing, training, workflows and handoffs.

Reporting 
- Maintain a weekly operations scorecard covering quality, service levels, capacity, staffing and delivery risks. 
- Turn performance data into clear actions, owners and deadlines, and own the department's quarterly priorities.

**What you'll bring**

* 3–5 years of direct people-management experience, including hiring, coaching, performance management and staffing decisions. Project leadership alone is not enough.
* Experience overseeing multiple operations functions, such as client service, new business and account opening, money movement, investment operations and financial planning support.
* Experience developing team leads or managers who run their own teams.
* A track record of building and scaling an operation, not only maintaining one: building processes, improving workflows, measuring capacity and putting the right staffing structure in place as the organization grew, with measurable improvements in turnaround time, accuracy, productivity or service levels.
* Experience leading operations or advisor services in wealth management at an RIA. Custodian candidates are welcome if they have led advisor-facing service operations and understand how independent RIAs operate across client service, new business and investment operations.
* Hands-on knowledge of advisory firm workflows: account opening, transfers, custodian requirements, client service and operational accuracy.
* RIA candidates: experience at a firm with more than $500M AUM. $1B+ is preferred.
* Experience leading remote teams.
* Direct, collaborative communication and confidence handling difficult performance conversations.

**Nice to have**

* Experience with Salesforce, Redtail and common custodian platforms.
* Workflow automation or process-improvement experience.
* Experience with a structured operating or accountability framework (for example EOS).

**Your first 90 days**

* Get to know the team and each client's delivery requirements.
* Assess immediate service, staffing and coverage risks.
* Clarify responsibilities and escalation paths across operations.
* Set baseline metrics and weekly reporting.
* Build a 60–90 day capacity forecast and a prioritized improvement plan.

**How to apply**

This search is confidential and is being handled by South Key. Company details will be shared with qualified candidates after an initial conversation.

Pay: $150,000.00 - $160,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Vision insurance

Work Location: Remote

Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies' core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

The Director of Manufacturing Automation leads the enterprise roadmap for practical, scalable automation across Karman manufacturing facilities. This leader partners with site operations, manufacturing engineering, quality, IT, and finance to identify high-return opportunities, pilot and deploy solutions, and sustain measurable improvements in safety, throughput, labor productivity, and quality. The role balances strategic technology selection with hands-on shop-floor execution and is accountable for standardizing successful solutions across multiple locations. 
 
**Responsibilities** 

* Develops and owns the enterprise manufacturing automation strategy, investment roadmap, and prioritized project portfolio.
* Identifies and quantifies automation opportunities through site assessments, capacity analysis, labor studies, and business cases with measurable returns.
* Leads implementation of robotics, CNC tending, automated inspection, material handling, and other fit-for-purpose production technologies.
* Partners with IT and cybersecurity teams on machine connectivity, industrial controls, data integrity, and secure integration with enterprise systems.
* Establishes standards for automation architecture, equipment acceptance, safety validation, commissioning, documentation, and maintainability.
* Coordinates cross-functional project teams and vendors to deliver automation installations within approved cost, schedule, and performance targets.
* Works with Quality and Engineering to validate automated processes, product conformity, and controlled changes in regulated manufacturing environments.
* Develops site technical capabilities through training, change management, and sustainable maintenance and support plans.
* Tracks automation performance using utilization, overall equipment effectiveness, cycle time, yield, labor hours, and realized financial benefits.
* Provides executive reporting on project status, risks, capital needs, and enterprise replication opportunities.

**Required Qualifications** 

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, manufacturing, automation, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
* 10+ years of manufacturing engineering, industrial automation, or related technical experience, including 5+ years leading complex projects or teams.
* Demonstrated deployment of industrial automation solutions in discrete manufacturing environments.
* Experience developing capital business cases, managing vendors, and delivering projects against financial and operational targets.
* Working knowledge of industrial controls, robotics, machine interfaces, functional safety, and production data systems.
* Ability to lead across multiple sites and influence stakeholders without direct reporting authority.

**Preferred Qualifications** 

* Aerospace and defense manufacturing experience, including AS9100-controlled production.
* Experience with CNC automation, automated inspection, machine monitoring, and ERP/MES integration.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or demonstrated continuous improvement leadership.
* Advanced engineering degree or professional automation certification.

**Special Mentions** 

* Travel of up to 50% is required to Karman manufacturing facilities, suppliers, and project locations, based on business needs.
* Future relocation to a designated Karman location may be required based on evolving business needs. Any relocation expectations will be discussed with the employee in advance.
* Ability to work in active manufacturing environments and follow all site safety, security, and controlled-information procedures.

**Physical Requirements** 

* Regularly moves between office, production, and manufacturing engineering areas and uses computers and standard office equipment.
* Occasionally stands and walks for extended periods during shop-floor reviews and equipment assessments.
* The essential functions of this position must be performed with or without reasonable accommodation.

**Measures of Success** 
Automation project return on investment; realized labor-hour savings; equipment utilization and uptime; throughput and cycle-time improvement; quality yield; project delivery to plan.

**Benefits** 

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid time off
* Health Savings Account (HSA) with company contribution
* Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
* Company-paid life and AD&D insurance
* Short- and long-term disability coverage
* Tuition reimbursement

Karman Space and Defense is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

**Position Overview**

Maltz Jupiter Theatre (MJT) is Florida's only LORT B+ regional theatre, with a 659-seat mainstage, the 198-seat Island Theatre, the Goldner Conservatory, the Wardrobe gift shop, VIP lounges and a growing campus. The Director of Operations becomes the single point of accountability for the building and the patron experience, from an air-conditioning issue, leaks to a sold-out opening night.

The Director of Operations is responsible for the day-to-day running of the Maltz Jupiter Theatre campus so that every performance, class, event and donor experience happens in a safe, clean, fully working building. This is a senior leadership role, not a hands-on trades role. The Director of Operations plans, assigns, follows up and is accountable for results, while maintenance staff, cleaners, House Managers and vendors execute the work.

The Director of Operations is responsible for the management, maintenance, safety and operational excellence of the Theatre's facilities, and develops and executes a long-term facilities plan for asset replacement, sustainability and risk management. This position reports to the Producing Artistic Director/Chief Executive.

**Key Responsibilities**

The Director of Operations is accountable for every area below. The work itself is executed by staff, volunteers and vendors whom the Director of Operations directs and follows up with.

1. Facilities and Building Systems

* Oversee the condition and performance of the entire Theatre including, but not limited to, the MainStage, Island Theatre, Goldner Conservatory, offices, lobbies, Wardrobe gift shop, Green Room Club Level, GR2 and future spaces such as the Scene.

* Oversee HVAC performance and response, including air-conditioning leaks, humidity, temperature complaints, and chiller and air-handler issues. Ensure root causes are repaired, not just the symptoms.

* Oversee roofing, plumbing, electrical, elevators, fire suppression, generators, non-theatrical lighting, doors and hardware, parking lot, landscaping and signage.

* Monitor moisture control and mold prevention, especially during dark periods, and coordinate professional remediation when needed.

* Build and execute a preventive maintenance calendar for all major systems, with service records, warranties, permits and equipment manuals kept current.

* Hold an annual facility condition review and recommend a multi-year capital repair and replacement plan to the Producing Artistic Director/Chief Executive and the Director of Finance and Administration.

* Maintain an asset inventory and forecast timely replacement of furniture, fixtures, carpeting, HVAC, lighting and equipment.

* Oversee environmental sustainability and energy efficiency initiatives.

2. Work Orders and Project Follow-Through

* Own the JotForm maintenance request system: Review each submission and ensure every request is logged, prioritized, assigned, tracked and closed.

* Review open requests daily and set response standards by urgency (for example, same-day for safety issues and leaks, 72 hours for routine repairs).

* Assign work to in-house maintenance and cleaning staff or the appropriate vendor, and confirm completion before a request is closed.

* Report weekly to leadership on open, overdue and completed work, and flag recurring problems.

* Manage small capital and renovation projects from scope through punch list, coordinating with contractors, designers and the Town as needed.

3. Vendors and Contracts

* Manage all building and operations vendors including, but not limited to, HVAC, janitorial supplies, pest control, elevator, fire and life safety, security monitoring, landscaping, waste and recycling, linens, bar and beverage suppliers, and others.

* Solicit bids, validate that contractors are licensed and insured, recommend vendors and negotiate service terms, with contracts executed through the Director of Finance and Administration.

* Hold vendors to service levels, track certificates of insurance and contract renewal dates.

* Approve vendor invoices for accuracy before they are provided to the Finance department for processing.

4. Front of House and Patron Experience

* Review incident and house reports after every performance.

* Ensure lobbies, restrooms, seating areas and accessible routes are clean, stocked and show-ready before doors open.

* Oversee ADA accommodations and assistive listening equipment in addition to the Front of House and Bar Manager, and serve as the escalation point for patron complaints about the facility or service.

* Coordinate with box office, development and marketing on opening nights, galas, donor events, the season announcement and community programs, as needed.

* Collaborate with Production on load-ins, load-outs and technical needs from a facilities perspective, and on scheduling building use among departments.

5. Bars, Concessions and Signature Experiences

* Supervise the Front of House and Bar Manger to ensure bar operations across the building are staffed, inventory is properly stocked, inventory counts are performed, cash handling with the Finance department, and liquor licensing and responsible-service compliance is maintained.

* Supervise the Building Facilities Manager who is responsible for room set ups and tear-downs for every event.

* Ensure the Front of House and Bar Manager delivers the operational side of Signature Experiences including, but not limited to, GR2, the Green Room Club Level Lounge, the future Scene, onstage seating packages and themed pre-show events, so the experience matches what was sold.

* Be available to fill in for the Front of House and Bar Manager in the event of an absence.

6. Volunteer Program (Indirect Oversight)

* Provide operational leadership for the Theatre’s 420 volunteers, working through the Volunteer Coordinator, who continues to recruit and schedule them.

* Ensure volunteers in operational roles (ushers, greeters, hospitality, event support) are trained in house procedures, safety and emergency protocols.

* Make sure staffing levels by performance and event match patron needs, and resolve conflicts between volunteer, staff and patron needs.

* Champion volunteer recognition alongside the Volunteer Coordinator.

7. Security, Access and Loss Prevention

* Oversee security systems including, but not limited to, alarms, access control, keys and building lock-up procedures.

* Work with the IT Manager on building security including cameras, access management, and workspace readiness (keys, access cards, phones and equipment) for new employee offices and visiting artists.

* Manage security staffing or contracted security for performances, galas and high-profile events.

* Investigate missing items, damage and building incidents. Maintain incident reports and coordinate with police and insurance as needed.

* Maintain the key and access register, issuing and revoking access as staff change.

* Manage and maintain the building-wide paging and communication systems.

8. Emergencies and On-Call Duty

* Serve as the primary on-call contact for the building 24/7, on a rotation with designated backups for nights off and vacations.

* Respond to alarms, leaks, power outages, break-ins and other after-hours events, and decide when to call vendors, police or fire.

* Oversee the Theatre’s emergency action plan as it relates to evacuation, severe weather and hurricane preparation and recovery, medical emergencies, active threat, and show-stop procedures.

* Run regular drills and training for staff, house managers and volunteers, and maintain emergency contact lists, evacuation plans, and first aid and AED readiness.

* Ensure the Producing Artistic Director/Chief Executive remains informed of any incident affecting safety, performances, donors or the press.

9. Safety and Compliance

* Serve as the Theatre's primary safety officer, ensuring the building meets fire code, life safety, OSHA, ADA, health department and occupancy requirements. Serve as lead for inspections with the fire marshal and the Town.

* Maintain safety data sheets, inspection logs, fire extinguisher and alarm testing records, and elevator certificates.

* Work with the Production department so front-of-house and building safety align with stage and backstage safety.

* Manage relationships with local emergency and law enforcement agencies.

* Partner with the Finance department on insurance renewals, claims and risk reviews.

10. Budget and Reporting

* Build and manage the operations, facilities, front-of-house and bar budgets, including annual and multi-year capital budgets, with the Director of Finance and Administration.

* Track spending against budget and identify potential savings in utilities, supplies and service contracts.

* Provide monthly operations reports to leadership and, when asked, to Board committees.

11. Staff Leadership and Cross-Department Coordination

* Hire, train, schedule, supervise and evaluate operations staff.

* Write and maintain standard operating procedures for building opening and closing, show days, events, rentals and emergencies.

* Lead a weekly operations meeting with production, box office, development, marketing, the Goldner Conservatory and the Volunteer Coordinator to review the week's calendar and building needs.

* Coordinate building use for rentals, community partners, Goldner Conservatory classes and camps, so every space is booked, set and turned over correctly.

12. Campus Growth

* Represent operations in planning for campus expansion, including visiting artist housing on the land across the street and new amenity spaces.

* Advise on maintainability, staffing and operating costs of new spaces before they open, and lead their move into day-to-day operation.

**Reporting Structure**

The Director of Operatins supervises the people who keep the building running and coordinates, without supervising, the people whose work depends on it.

**Direct reports**

Building Facilities Manager, Front of House Manager, contracted security

**Indirect / dotted-line**

Volunteer Coordinator (for operational volunteer roles); about 420 volunteers through the Coordinator, House Manager, House Attendants

**Key partners**

Director of Finance and Administration; Production and Technical Direction; Box Office; Development; Marketing; Goldner Conservatory

**External**

Building and service vendors, contractors, Town of Jupiter, fire marshal, police, insurance carriers

**QualificationsRequired**

* 5-7+ years of progressive experience in facilities, venue or operations management, with at least 3 years supervising staff and vendors.

* Experience running a performing arts center, theatre, arena, museum, hotel or similar public venue with large audiences.

* Working knowledge of HVAC, electrical, plumbing, life safety and building automation systems, enough to judge vendor recommendations and costs.

* Proven record of running a work-order or ticketing system and closing work reliably.

* Experience with project management, capital planning, and building and managing operating budgets and vendor contracts.

* Strong leadership, written and verbal communication, and organizational skills, with staff, board members, donors, patrons, visiting artists and contractors.

* Calm, decisive judgment in emergencies; comfortable being the person everyone calls.

* Ability to balance strategic planning with hands-on problem solving, to be self-directed, and to manage multiple projects in a fast-paced environment.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Outlook, Word and Excel, and online forms such as JotForm.

* Valid driver's license; ability to pass a background check; able to respond to the Theatre within about 30 minutes when on call.

* Professional conduct at all times, representing the Theatre positively to artists, partner organizations, vendors, donors, volunteers, patrons and Board members.

**Preferred**

* Bachelor's degree in facilities management, business, hospitality or arts administration, or equivalent experience.

* Certifications such as Facility Management Professional (FMP), Certified Facility Manager (CFM), OSHA 30, CPR/AED and first aid, and crowd management training.

* Experience with safety management and emergency preparedness protocols.

* Background in facilities management software or CMMS systems, and in LEED or sustainable facility practices.

* Front-of-house or hospitality leadership, including liquor service compliance.

* Experience with hurricane preparation and recovery in Florida.

* Experience working with volunteers in a nonprofit setting.

* Familiarity with theatre operations, production schedules and event logistics.

**Working Conditions**

* Schedule follows the Theatre and may include evenings, weekends and holidays, with a regular presence at performances and major events.

* On call 24/7 on a published rotation, including during hurricanes and other emergencies.

* Walks the full campus daily, climbs stairs and ladders, enters mechanical rooms and roof areas, and lifts up to 40 pounds occasionally.

Pay: $85,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

Capitol Aggregates, a division of Zachry, stands on a rich tradition of creativity, stability, innovation, and experience in the construction and building materials industry. Fully understanding that Capitols employees are the heart of our success, we foster a dynamic work environment by providing development opportunities such as training, education, and career advancement.

We believe people are our greatest asset and offer a variety of training and development opportunities to promote excellence and facilitate career advancement. We take care of our team members as family, within a culture of service where we do the right thing because it is the right thing to do.

**Our Core Values guide everything we do:**

Every Person Matters | Together We Can Do Great Things | This Is More Than a Job

**Position Overview**

The Plant Manager is responsible for overseeing the overall production, safety, maintenance, and employee management activities at the aggregate operations site. This role ensures operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and a strong culture of safety and environmental stewardship. The Plant Manager leads all aspects of site performance with a hands-on, collaborative approach, ensuring operational goals are met while building a high-performing team and delivering strong customer service.

* Lead, plan, and direct daily plant operations including production, maintenance, and material handling.
* Manage production schedules, inventory controls, and key cost drivers to meet operational and financial targets.
* Lead employee life cycle activities including hiring, training, coaching, and performance management.
* Establish and enforce a strong safety culture ensuring compliance with MSHA, OSHA, environmental, and company standards.
* Monitor plant performance, operating costs, and efficiency to drive continuous improvement.
* Provide regular performance updates and strategic input to the Area Manager.

NOTE: This list presents only the principal duties of the position and is not intended to be comprehensive. Other duties and responsibilities may be assigned as dictated by the business needs and conditions. As an essential function of the job, good attendance is required.

**What Youll Bring**

**Required Skills and Abilities**

* Strong operational knowledge of aggregate production and equipment maintenance.
* Working knowledge of MSHA, OSHA, and environmental regulations.
* Proven ability to lead teams, set priorities, and deliver results.
* Strong problem-solving, organizational, and decision-making skills.
* Demonstrated commitment to safety leadership and operational excellence.

**Education & Experience**

* High School Diploma or GED required.
* Associate degree in Leadership, Supervision, Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field preferred.
* 1015 years of progressive experience in aggregates, mining, or heavy industrial operations required.
* 510 years of experience leading and managing teams in a plant or operations setting required.
* 35 years of direct maintenance experience within a plant environment required.
* Familiarity with the operation of mobile heavy equipment preferred.

**Other Qualifications**

* Consistent enforcement of safe work practices and PPE usage.
* Ability to interpret safety regulations, equipment manuals, and operational standards.
* Adaptability to changing operational demands and a collaborative, team-oriented approach.

**Leadership Expectations**

* Communicate the companys vision and values clearly to employees.
* Lead with integrity, professionalism, and sound judgment.
* Inspire a culture of safety, accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
* Serve as a mentor and role model within the plant.

**Benefits & Equal Opportunity**

Capitol Aggregates offers an industry leading benefits package for our employees and their families.

* Medical, Dental, Vision and Life Insurance
* 401K, Paid Leave and Bonus Program
* Company-paid short-term and long-term disability insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Tuition Reimbursement
* And many more

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, disability, veteran status, or other legally protected status.

**Notice to Staffing Agencies**

Capitol Aggregates Inc. (Capitol) will not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from a candidate. Any unsolicited resumes sent to Capitol, including unsolicited resumes sent to a Capitol mailing address or email address, directly to Capitol employees, or to Capitols resume database, will be considered Capitol property. Capitol will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume. Capitol will consider any candidate for whom an Agency has submitted an unsolicited resume to have been referred by the Agency free of any charges or fees. Agencies must obtain advance written approval from Capitols recruiting function to submit resumes, and then only in conjunction with a valid, fully executed contract for service and in response to a specific job opening. Capitol will not pay a fee to any Agency that does not have such an agreement in place. No other Capitol employee is authorized to bind Capitol to any agreement regarding the placement of candidates by an Agency.

**Overview**

Lead the development and execution of the organization's Continuous Improvement strategy across manufacturing operations. Drive a culture of Operational Excellence through Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma methodologies, waste elimination, process standardization, employee engagement, and data-driven decision making. Partner with factory leadership to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity while supporting the growth and scalability of luxury furniture manufacturing operations.

**Responsibilities**

* Develop and deploy a comprehensive Continuous Improvement roadmap aligned with company strategic objectives.
* Serve as the Lean Manufacturing subject matter expert and champion Operational Excellence initiatives throughout the organization.
* Lead Kaizen events, Rapid Improvement Workshops, Gemba walks, Value Stream Mapping activities, and cross-functional improvement projects.
* Drive measurable improvements in Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, and Morale (SQDCM).
* Identify and eliminate waste utilizing Lean principles, including Transportation, Inventory, Motion, Waiting, Overproduction, Overprocessing, Defects, and Underutilized Talent.
* Establish and sustain standardized work, visual management systems, layered audits, and accountability processes.
* Facilitate implementation and sustainment of 5S and workplace organization initiatives across all departments.
* Develop Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), scorecards, dashboards, and reporting systems to monitor operational performance.
* Utilize root cause analysis methodologies including A3 Problem Solving, 5 Whys, Fishbone Diagrams, and Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA).
* Lead process improvement projects focused on throughput, labor efficiency, productivity, quality, material flow, inventory optimization, and lead-time reduction.

* Drive employee engagement through CI training, mentoring, coaching, and change management initiatives.
* Develop future CI leaders and establish a culture of continuous learning and problem-solving.
* Identify opportunities to improve Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), capacity utilization, and operational throughput.
* Evaluate and implement best practices related to Lean Enterprise systems and manufacturing excellence.
* Support facility expansion, capital projects, new product launches, and operational scaling activities.
* Present improvement plans and results to executive leadership using data-driven analysis.
* Provide leadership for strategic initiatives focused on cost reduction, quality enhancement, associate development, and customer satisfaction.

**Requirements**

* 10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations Management, Business Administration, or related field.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Master Black Belt Certification.
* 5+ years leading Continuous Improvement, Lean Manufacturing, Operational Excellence, Industrial Engineering, or related initiatives.
* Demonstrated success implementing Lean transformations and culture change initiatives in manufacturing environments.

* Demonstrated leadership of multi-site Continuous Improvement, Lean Manufacturing, and Operational Excellence initiatives strongly preferred.
* Strong knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Toyota Production System (TPS), Six Sigma, and Operational Excellence methodologies.
* Proven ability to lead enterprise-wide culture transformation initiatives.
* Advanced knowledge of Value Stream Mapping, Standard Work, Kanban, Pull Systems, Heijunka,SMED, Poka-Yoke, TPM, and Visual Management.
* Strong project management, organizational, and communication skills.
* Exceptional analytical and problem-solving abilities.
* Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.
* Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Power BI, and data analysis tools.
* Strong financial acumen with the ability to quantify business impact and ROI.
* Ability to influence and lead through all levels of the organization.
* Experience leading cross-functional teams without direct authority.
* Demonstrated change management and coaching skills.
* Ability to prioritize multiple strategic initiatives in a fast-paced environment.
* Must be able to work effectively within production and office environments.
* Must be able to walk, stand, and observe production processes for extended periods.
* Must be able to occasionally lift to 30 pounds.
* Must be able to wear required PPE while in manufacturing areas.
* Must adhere to all company safety standards and procedures.
* Must be committed to a culture of safety, accountability, respect, and continuous improvement.

* Ensures consistent compliance with standard operating procedures, policies, internal audit controls, Sarbanes-Oxley controls, and business management quality system requirements
* Analyze current operational processes and performance, recommending solutions for improvement when necessary.

**Department**
--------------

College of Aerospace, Computing, Engineering, and Design

**About the University**

 

Established in 1965, Metropolitan State University ( MSU Denver ) was founded to serve students who were underrepresented in higher education whose life paths and experiences did not fit the traditional mold. Sixty years later, the University continues to serve over 16,000 of Colorado’s extraordinary and diverse students, providing them with the foundation on which to build their unique aspirations. As the third largest public institution of higher education in Colorado, MSU Denver is a model university for today’s college students.

Proud of its federal designation as a Hispanic-Serving Institution that also offers graduate programs (gHSI) and the only Seal of Excelencia certified institution in Colorado, the University serves the most diverse undergraduate student population in the state, as well as the most first-generation students. Through affordable, flexible, and holistic education, MSU Denver helps students build essential skills grounded in a multicultural and global perspective that lead to undergraduate and graduate degrees, and career and life success.

 

At MSU Denver, we are committed to our CADRE values: Community, Access, Diversity, Respect, and Excellence. We strive to create a supportive and inclusive environment where all community members are valued and belong. Our dedication to breaking down barriers to education, fostering open dialogue, and promoting world-class scholarship ensures that we provide exceptional services and innovative learning opportunities for our students, faculty, and staff.

 

**Position Summary**

 

MSU Denver seeks a Director to lead the Advanced Manufacturing Sciences Institute ( AMSI ) and advance its development into a sustainable, impactful program. The Director manages all AMSI activities including the Industry 4.0 Center of Excellence which serves Colorado manufacturers through technology demonstrations, training, micro-credentials, and sponsored partnerships. The Director is the primary liaison and point of contact for all industry partners. The Director develops and maintains the Advanced Manufacturing Sciences academic programs in collaboration with various academic departments.

The Director builds integrated pathways for both degree-seeking students and non-degree learners. These pathways connect credentials, work-based learning, undergraduate and graduate programs, and lifelong learning. The Director also makes AMSI a hub for interdisciplinary collaboration within CACED and across the University. Through AMSI, the Director connects academic programs, faculty, students, industry partners, and community organizations around shared learning, applied research, workforce development, and emerging opportunities.

A high priority for the Director is to develop a long-term model that allows AMSI to sustain and grow its programs and activities beyond short-term or one-time funding. The incoming Director will build appropriate revenue-generating activities to support students, programs, equipment, and future growth.

 

**Responsibilities**

 

Institute Strategy

* Set and carry out AMSI’s mission, vision, and annual plan consistent with the strategy, budgets, goals, and policies of CACED and the University.
* Advance industry-relevant technologies, practices, and partnerships that prepare students to contribute from their first day on the job and that address manufacturing workforce gaps.
Maintain an active Advisory Board and keep it informed through an outcomes dashboard that tracks sponsors, student credit hours, enrollments, non-degree learners served, placements, revenue by source, and other appropriate data. 

Institute Sustainability

* Develop a long-term sustainability model and a multi-year business plan that sets out AMSI’s costs, funding sources, and revenue sources; update the plan each year.
* Build a diversified funding base that combines earned revenue, industry partnerships and sponsorships, philanthropy, and public and private grants.
* Develop appropriate revenue-generating activities that are consistent with the University’s mission and strategic plan.
* Oversee fee-based manufacturing services offered by AMSI.
* Pursue grants and other funding that build lasting capacity and plan how successful grant-funded programs and positions will continue after the award ends.
Partner with the Office of Sponsored Research and Projects and Advancement on identifying and applying for grants, gifts, corporate sponsorships, equipment and donations. 

Integrated Learning Pathways

* Work with faculty and academic departments to identify where micro-credentials, industry-recognized credentials, and competency-based training can be included in academic certificates and degrees consistent with University curriculum and credit policies.
* Expand work-based learning with manufacturing employers including internships, apprenticeships, industry-sponsored capstones, and applied projects.
* Strengthen the path from AMS undergraduate programs into graduate study and 4+1 programs.
* Create upskilling and reskilling training opportunities for incumbent workers and adult learners that offer clear entry points into credit-bearing programs.
Establish transfer and articulation agreements with community colleges and other educational partners. 

Interdisciplinary Collaboration

* Bring faculty and students from CACED’s aerospace, computing, engineering, and design programs, and from other appropriate academic programs, together with industry partners on sponsored projects, capstones, applied research, and grant proposals.
* Open AMSI’s labs, equipment, and industry relationships to academic programs across the University for teaching and applied research opportunities.
Host and participate in convenings and working groups that bring faculty, students, industry partners, and community organizations together on workforce development and emerging technologies. 

Industry 4.0 Center of Excellence

* Lead and grow the COE’s fee-for-service and manufacturing services programs through technology demonstrations, corporate training (standard and custom), micro-credentials and certificates, applied research and development, capstone sponsorships, and selective lab and equipment access.
* Draw on manufacturing networks including CAMA, WiM, Manufacturer’s Edge, and MWAMA, and on state and federal funding opportunities, to convene industry partners, launch programs, and generate applied industry projects.
Standardize scoping, intellectual property, safety, and performance-metric templates for company projects. 

Academic Programs

* Develop and maintain the AMS academic programs with faculty and department leaders and keep curricula current with industry needs through regular input from industry partners.
* Oversee student recruitment, retention, and job placement goals and activities.
Coordinate internship placements, serve as internship advisor, and manage internship evaluations and reporting. 

Laboratory Operations

* Oversee AMSI labs and testbeds for safe, scheduled use by multiple academic programs and expand their use for industry collaboration and applied research.
Plan equipment maintenance, upgrades, and replacement so that AMSI’s technology stays current with industry practice. 

Administration

* Supervise, evaluate, and develop AMSI staff and direct their work on the Institute’s priorities in lab operations, business operations, workforce development initiatives, student recruitment and retention, and marketing and communications.
* Prepare annual reports, budget plans, and periodic reviews and maintain sound financial management and risk controls.
Manage memoranda of understanding and other agreements with academic units and external partners. 

 

**Position Competencies**

* Champions CADRE values-based leadership and creates a positive workplace culture, by setting expectations, eliciting feedback and coaching across departments, ensuring accountability and excelling in conflict management
* Aligns operations across teams by optimizing resources, maintaining compliance, and empowering leaders to deliver consistent, measurable outcomes
* Translates University strategy into coordinated action by guiding decision-making, prioritizing initiatives, and adjusting plans to drive long-term progress
* Builds cross-functional partnerships, sharing information widely and facilitating dialogue to break down silos and advance University goals
* Creates a positive workplace culture of belonging by embedding equitable leadership and talent processes, fostering feedback and holding leaders accountable
Drives innovation by aligning initiatives to University priorities, anticipating change, and empowering leaders to implement sustainable improvements 

 

**Required Qualifications**

* Master’s degree from an accredited institution or an equivalent combination of education and experience
* Working knowledge of advanced manufacturing technologies and the workforce needs of manufacturing employers
* Familiarity with Colorado’s manufacturing employers, industry associations, and workforce funding programs
Experience supervising staff and managing budgets that draw on multiple funding sources, such as grants, contracts, gifts, or earned revenue 

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience building credential programs, apprenticeships, or other work-based learning that connects to degree programs
* A record of leading interdisciplinary initiatives with faculty and partners from multiple disciplines or organizations
* Experience securing state, federal, or foundation grants, and sustaining programs after grant funding ends
* Industry experience in manufacturing, aerospace, or a related sector
Experience in higher education with diverse, urban student populations 

 

We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every preferred qualification. We are most interested in finding the candidate who will best contribute to the AMSI Institute, our mission, and the University.

**Schedule Information**

* Full time, 40 hrs/wk
* Exempt
* Days of the Week: Monday - Friday, during regular University business hours that typically range between 8:00 am - 5:00 pm
* Evenings and Weekend Work: As needed for industry events, University events, meetings, and other program activities
* Schedule: Primarily in person on campus with some flexibility for remote work depending upon program needs and supervisor approval
Travel: Local travel as needed for industry partnerships, employer engagement, and related activities, with occasional travel for conferences or professional development 

 

**Salary for Announcement**

 

Under Colorado law, MSU Denver is required to provide a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role and should not offer a salary outside of the range posted in this job announcement. This range takes into account a variety of factors including but not limited to experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, analysis of internal equity, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be offered a salary at or near the top of the range for a position. Salary offers are determined based on final candidate qualifications and experience.

 

The anticipated hiring range that the university reasonably expects to pay for this position is $115,000 - $130,000.

 

This position is paid monthly and is eligible for MSU Denver benefits .

 

**Conditions of Appointment**

 

MSU Denver does not offer H-1B or other work authorization visa sponsorship for this position. Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States at the time of hire and maintain work authorization throughout the employment term.

 

**Instructions to Apply**

 

Please apply by visiting our career site and searching for JR105958: https://www.msudenver.edu/careers/ .

 

The following documents are required to be included with your application:

* Resume
* Cover letter describing relevant job experiences as they relate to listed job qualifications and interest in the position
A list of three professional references and their contact information (at least one reference provided must be a supervisor, either current or former). 

 

Please ensure you have uploaded all required documents into the Resume/Cover letter section of the application.

 

Official transcripts will be required of the candidate selected for hire.

 

**Deadline**

 

Applications accepted until position is filled; priority given to applications received by Monday, December 7, 2026 at 11:59 PM MST.

**Closing Date**
----------------

Open Until Filled

**Posting Representative**
--------------------------

Tanya Rogowsky

**Posting Representative Email**
--------------------------------

trogowsk@msudenver.edu
 

**Benefits**
------------

The University’s benefits package is comprehensive and offers medical, vision and dental, free RTD pass, tuition reimbursement, as well as a life and supplemental insurance plans, retirement plans and other programs, such as access to a long-term disability (LTD) plan. Visit MSU Denver’s benefits website to learn more.

 

For a brief overview, please see: https://www.msudenver.edu/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/MSU-Benefit-Summary.pdf .

 

The University will provide reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities throughout the employment application process. To request an accommodation pursuant to the Americans with Disabilities Act, please contact the Human Resources ADA Coordinator at totalrewards@msudenver.edu .

 

**Background Checks**

Metropolitan State University of Denver is dedicated to ensuring a safe and secure environment for our faculty, staff, students, and visitors. To Assist in achieving that goal, we conduct background checks on all finalists for positions at the University prior to employment.

 

**Diversity Statement**
-----------------------

Metropolitan State University of Denver is a unique, access-oriented campus community that values diversity, equity, and inclusion in all its forms. Our student population consists of nearly 58% first generation students and over 50% students of color. We are a designated Hispanic Serving Institution located in downtown Denver.

 

We create an equitable learning and working environment in concert with individuals who consistently demonstrate commitment to equity and inclusion. We greatly value the diverse identities and perspectives of our students, faculty, and staff and recognize that in order to achieve a just and equitable society, diversity must go beyond simple representation. It requires critical inquiry and dialogue and a commitment to action. We strive to provide a culture of belonging for all community members to achieve personal and professional success.

**Premier Linen Services | Fort Myers, FL | Full-Time | $85,000 – $125,000 per year**

**About us** 
Premier Linen Services runs an advanced, state-of-the-art commercial laundry facility serving large and luxury hospitality properties across Florida. We’re a growing, owner-led company with a modern, high-volume plant, and we’re looking for a hands-on leader to keep it running safely and efficiently every day.

**About the role** 
The Plant Manager runs daily operations across our production facility. You’ll keep production moving through washing, drying, finishing and packaging, work with maintenance and logistics, and lead a team focused on quality, safety and on-time delivery.

What you’ll do

**LOCATION: Raleigh, NC (Hybrid)**

**Who we are?**

Built on more than a century of innovation and decades of substation expertise, **Linxon** blends AtkinsRéalis' project management strength with Hitachi Energy's technological leadership. Together, we deliver high‑performing EPC solutions that strengthen the power grid.

We support community growth and industrial development by providing end‑to‑end engineering, procurement, management, and construction services for complex AC substation and electrification projects across five core markets.

**What We Believe?**

We believe in the value of every client's'investment and take pride in tackling challenging, high‑risk projects. With deep expertise and continuous development, our teams operate with the precision, resilience, and mission‑focus needed to deliver crucial infrastructure—often described as the "special forces" of our industry.

To learn more about us click on the link below:

Careers - Linxon

 

**How will you make your impact?**

As the **Head of Quality,** you will leader to define, implement, and continuously improve the Quality Management System across the Americas. This role is responsible for ensuring quality is designed into every stage of project delivery, from engineering and procurement through construction, commissioning, and closeout. This is a highly visible leadership role with direct influence on project performance, supplier quality, operational discipline, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement across the Americas.

The **Head of Quality** will establish and lead a quality organization that embeds quality into how projects are planned, executed, and continuously improved.

You will drive a preventive approach to quality by strengthening planning, supplier oversight, project controls, auditing, and lessons learned. You will create the frameworks that connect Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Project Delivery, and Quality into a single system focused on delivering projects right the first time. Success will be measured by reductions in rework and recurring issues, stronger supplier performance, improved audit outcomes, increased first-time-right execution, and the maturity of the quality culture across the organization.

**What will you do?**

 

* You will lead the development and continuous improvement of the Americas Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring consistent standards, governance, and accountability across the region.
* You will establish quality requirements and controls from tender through project closeout to ensure quality is built into project delivery from the outset.
* You will implement risk-based supplier qualification, surveillance, inspection, and release processes to improve supplier quality performance.
* You will ensure inspection and test plans align with engineering requirements, contract obligations, and construction execution strategies.
* You will lead audits, management reviews, quality assurance programs, and performance reporting across the project portfolio.
* You will drive root-cause analysis and corrective action processes that address systemic issues rather than isolated events.
* You will establish and lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on reducing defects, rework, and the Cost of Poor Quality.
* You will build and develop a high-performing Quality Assurance and Quality Control organization across the Americas.
* You will strengthen collaboration across Engineering, Procurement, PMO, Construction, and HSE to improve quality outcomes throughout the project lifecycle.
* You will develop quality capability, training programs, succession plans, and best practices that support long-term organizational growth.
* You will assess and strengthen the Americas Quality Management System, focusing resources on the highest-priority risks and improvement opportunities.
* You will establish clear quality governance, accountability, and performance reporting across the region.
* You will standardize project quality planning, supplier quality management, inspection requirements, and NCR governance practices.
* You will improve visibility into the Cost of Poor Quality, quality trends, and leading indicators across the project portfolio.
* You will reduce recurring quality issues, rework, and warranty exposure through stronger preventive controls and root-cause resolution.
* You will improve audit performance, supplier quality outcomes, and project readiness before execution begins.
* You will create a culture where quality is proactively planned, owned, measured, and continuously improved across functions.
* You will build a scalable quality organization capable of supporting Linxon's continued growth across the Americas.

**Who you are?**

 

* You are an experienced quality leader with 7-15+ years of experience in EPC, power, industrial, construction, manufacturing, or other complex project environments.
* You are proven in leading multi-project or regional Quality Management Systems and driving quality performance across diverse operations.
* You are knowledgeable in ISO 9001 principles, supplier quality management, project QA/QC, auditing practices, and root-cause methodologies.
* You are skilled at translating quality data and performance trends into preventive actions, operational discipline, and business improvements.
* You are experienced in developing quality organizations, improving governance, and building sustainable quality cultures.
* You hold a degree in engineering, quality, or a related technical field, and quality or auditing certifications are considered an asset.
* You are a leader who puts the mission, the customer, and the team ahead of individual recognition.
* You are comfortable making decisions with incomplete information and adjusting course as conditions change.
* You are committed to raising standards while fostering respect, inclusion, and psychological safety.
* You are passionate about developing people, sharing knowledge, and strengthening organizational capability.
* You are trusted because of your actions, credibility, and follow-through rather than your title.
* You are disciplined, data-driven, and focused on creating systems that prevent issues rather than simply react to them.

We are looking for a leader who understands the unique demands of the promotional products and custom merchandise industry — where every day can involve changing order volumes, customized products, tight deadlines, multiple production methods, material constraints, and constantly shifting priorities. The ideal candidate has experience leading production in promotional products, decorated apparel, custom merchandise, commercial printing, signage, embroidery, DTF/DTG, screen printing, heat transfer, or a similar high-mix production environment. You will own the operational performance of the manufacturing organization and work closely with leadership and other departments to build a reliable, scalable, high-performing production operation. As Head of Manufacturing, you will be responsible for translating customer demand into an efficient production operation. You will lead the people, processes, equipment, materials, and systems required to consistently deliver orders on time, at the expected quality, and at the right cost. You will be expected to identify bottlenecks before they become problems, establish clear accountability across the production team, and continuously improve how work moves through the facility. Responsibilities Production & Operations - Own daily production operations and overall manufacturing performance. - Plan and prioritize production based on order volume, deadlines, capacity, materials, and available labor. - Establish production schedules and adjust priorities as demand changes. - Monitor throughput, turnaround time, capacity utilization, labor efficiency, quality, and waste. - Identify production bottlenecks and implement corrective actions. - Ensure orders move efficiently from intake through production, quality control, and fulfillment.
